sentences.text: Pampadromaeus was a small, bipedal animal that exhibits a mosaic of both basal and derived traits.
Its anatomy included a much longer lower leg than thighbone, indicating it was adapted for running.
The animal possessed a total of eighty-eight teeth, with four located in the premaxilla and about twenty in the maxilla and lower jaw.
A 2022 study found that Pampadromaeus lacked an invasive air sac system and its bones were not pneumatised.
The generic name Pampadromaeus combines the Quechua word for 'plain' and the Greek word for 'runner'.
The specific name barberenai honors the Brazilian paleontologist Mário Costa Barberena.

The genus Pampadromaeus was described by Cabreira et al. in 2011, named by Sergio F. Cabreira, Cesar L. Schultz, Jonathas S. Bittencourt, Marina B. Soares, Daniel C. Fortier, Lúcio R. Silva, and Max C. Langer.
Pampadromaeus is known only from a single holotype specimen, ULBRA-PVT016, which is a partial but well-preserved skeleton.

Cladistic analyses have identified Pampadromaeus as a basal sauropodomorph, though researchers note that this classification is not strongly supported due to difficulties in determining its affinities with early dinosaur groups.
The species is classified within the parent group Saturnaliidae, belongs to the family Saturnaliidae, and is classified in the class Saurischia.
